summary: Windsor County, VT tower from 1920; the Herald says it was sold and moved to Topsham in 1973, and no source places the structure today.

access.note: Mt. Cushman State Forest is landlocked, and the state says there is no legal public access to it. The summit is not part of the forest.

facts.status_note: Tower gone; the Herald says it was sold and moved to Topsham in 1973.

Bethel Courier (Oct 4, 1934) reports a planned steel tower built by CCC crews, with the platform 45 ft 9 in up; the Herald dates a 50-foot tower to the 1920s, so the dates disagree
Will Stone, fire warden for 16 years by April 1946 (article of April 3, 1946)
Will Stone begins his 20th season (Herald, April 8, 1948); the 16-year count from 1946 does not fit one unbroken run of seasons
Biennial reports for 1949-50: stairs and cabin floor painted, new cap installed on tower
Tug Vinton is the fire watcher (July 25, 1952); in August 1952 Rochester townspeople planned a weekend road to the tower
New cabin built under a replacement program
Sold and moved to Topsham, per the Herald; no source found for where the structure stands now

notes_for_editor: No NHLR or FFLOS register entry was found for Mount Cushman. Sources conflict on the second tower: a 1934 newspaper item describes a planned steel tower built by CCC crews, while the Herald describes a 1920s tower 50 feet tall. The 1920 first tower is supported by three sources. The Herald's account of a 1973 sale and move to Topsham is a single source and is unverified; the FFLA list shows a relocated Mount Ascutney tower in West Topsham, which is a different structure and is not used. The 1934 item also names a fire tower on 'Cushing Mountain' in Rochester, which is not used. The record's county typo 'Windson' also appears on the FFLA list. Stone's counts conflict: 16 years by April 1946 and a 20th season in April 1948 do not fit one unbroken run of seasons, so the story says the counts do not agree. The 1934 item's 45 ft 9 in is platform height, so the story does not treat it as a height conflict with the Herald's 50 ft.
